content:
Chapter practice tells you what your child knows; a mixed paper tells you what they can DO in 60 minutes. The real IMO never asks thirty integer questions in a row — it hops from percentages to angles to a reasoning puzzle, and that switching is a skill of its own. Take the free IMO Class 7 practice test below: 10 questions drawn from ten different Class 7 chapters, with instant scoring and worked explanations.

Why mixed practice beats one more chapter revision

  • The real paper switches topics every question — chapter-order practice never trains that.
  • Mixed tests expose the chapter your child avoids (everyone has one).
  • Timing only becomes real against a full 30-question paper.
  • Confidence on exam day comes from having "been here before" — twenty-five times.

How to use this free test

  • Attempt all 10 in one sitting, without help.
  • Score 8+ — move to full-length papers. Score below 6 — revise the weakest chapter first.
  • Read every explanation, including for correct answers.
  • Note the time taken. Ten mixed questions in under 12 minutes is Olympiad pace; under 15 is solid; over 20 means the weak chapter is stealing time from the strong ones.

Free IMO Class 7 practice test

The quiz below mixes Integers, Rational Numbers, Algebra, Ratio, Percentages, Geometry, Data Handling and Reasoning — exactly the spread of a real IMO paper.

Then do the real thing — 25 times

The IMO Class 7 Maths — 25 Practice Papers e-book has 25 full-length papers (750 MCQs), every paper balanced across all 18 chapters, with an answer key after each paper and step-by-step solutions for all 750 questions — including diagram questions, exactly like the exam. Chapter-wise drills are on the Grade 7 Math shelf, and the theory is free on the vidaara.org IMO course.

questions.q: What is the sum of 3/5 and −2/7?
If A = 3x<sup>2</sup> + 2x − 7 and B = −x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 4, find A + B.
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> terms: 3 − 1 = 2. x terms: 2 + 5 = 7. Constants: −7 + 4 = −3. A + B = 2x<sup>2</sup> + 7x − 3.

questions.q: The number subtracted from each term of 17 : 33 to give 7 : 15 is:
When 35% of a number is subtracted from the number itself, the result is 520. The number is:
An angle equals one-fourth of its supplement. The angle is:
questions.explanation: x = ¼(180 − x); multiply by 4: 4x = 180 − x. 5x = 180, so x = 36°.

questions.q: A wire of length 480 cm forming a square is rebent into a rectangle of length 140 cm. The breadth is:
With a scale of 1 unit = 15 students, a bar of height 7.5 units represents:

questions.explanation: All the others are multiples of 12.
